bugs.text: The challenging stage soft-locks. After wave 5, nextChallengeWave returns before filtering 'gone' enemies, so enemies.length never reaches 0 and the game sits forever on an empty stage 3 unless all 8 of the last wave are destroyed.
Off-by-one lives. The game ends when the reserve count reaches 0, so the player gets 2 ships instead of 3 (the bot's first game ended within 30 s).
The two-shot limit is per x position and Space auto-fires every frame. Moving while firing sprays staircases of bullets (visible in the play screenshots); each tap fires 2+ shots.
chHits and chBonus are never incremented, so wave bonus, PERFECT and NUMBER OF HITS never work; the bonus display also has an operator-precedence bug (755).
READY text can never show (needs invuln>2, but invuln starts at 2).
The dual fighter is two overlapping sprites 6 px apart with a 12 px hitbox, and it is lost at every stage start because startStage calls resetPlayer.
The captured fighter never fires at the player.
Stage badges always show one identical flag for stages 1-6; denominations are not represented.
Entering enemies fly to the raw slot, then snap up to 14 px to the swayed slot position.
A single fighter is drawn at x-3, but its shots come from x, 3 px off the nose.
A dual-fighter hit removes the half chosen by the last bullet in the array, not the bullet that hit.
Escorts of a tractor-beam boss stop at y=150, then jump to the top of the screen to return.

summary: A compact, cleanly sectioned single-file clone with a proper fixed-timestep loop, pixel-art sprites, a pixel font, synthesized sound and most of the Galaga skeleton: curved group entries, a swaying and breathing formation, curved dives that wrap from the bottom to the top, boss escorts, a working tractor-beam capture/rescue/hostile flow, and a results screen. Stages 1-2 play reasonably, but several core rules are wrong. The player gets only two ships. The two-shot limit is bypassed by moving, producing visible bullet streams. READY never appears. The dual fighter is two overlapping sprites and disappears at the next stage. The captured fighter never shoots. Badges never show denominations. Most damaging: the challenging stage never counts hits or awards its bonuses and soft-locks after its last wave unless every enemy in it is shot, so progress normally stops at stage 3. The sprites are recoloured copies of one humanoid shape rather than recognisable bees, butterflies and bosses, which hurts the Galaga feel.
